The slack variable update is written as u_i(t+1) = u_i(t) + η_p (ρ u_i(t) − λ_i(t)). The correct gradient descent direction for minimizing the Lagrangian with respect to u_i (objective includes (ρ/2)u_i² − λ_i u_i) is u_i ← u_i − η_p (ρ u_i − λ_i) = u_i + η_p(λ_i − ρ u_i). The given update uses (ρ u_i − λ_i) with an addition, which is gradient ascent, not descent. The algorithm is therefore incorrect and will not properly optimize the resilient constraint problem.

The binary definition is never used; the method relies on continuous γ. This is an internal inconsistency that complicates the interpretation of the model.

The conclusion states: "ACE consistently and significantly accelerates training, boosts sample efficiency, and achieves unmatched accuracy and robustness relative to all existing methods — without any need for manual tuning or domain overhead." This is a vast overstatement. The experiments show mixed results (e.g., small improvements on QM9 for SEGNN, significant training overhead from extra parameters, Table 4 missing data). Moreover, hyperparameter tuning (learning rates ηp, ηd, grid search) is still required, as shown in the appendix. The claim of "unmatched accuracy" and "revolutionizes equivariant deep learning" is unsupported and exaggerated.

The abstract states that ACE provides "improvements in select settings", whereas the conclusion claims "consistently and significantly accelerates training, boosts sample efficiency, and achieves unmatched accuracy and robustness relative to all existing methods". These two statements directly contradict each other on the generality and strength of the results.
